plan.title: bug(scope): a story brief that names several issues cannot pass both closing-keywords and the completion identity join

narratives.Description: A story brief can name several issues. Before merge the closing-keywords check asks the product PR for a story line for every issue the brief names, and the writer writes a full deft-story mark for each; after merge the completion identity join needs one sole mark, so a multi-issue story needs an operator delivery-identity-attest grant. This story makes the check and the writer ask for one line per running brief, for the issue the completion join anchors on (resolvePlanGithubIssueRef), and adds one refusal inside the story-line check when the plan-id adopter's owner list for that issue names a different brief, or is empty while the brief owns another of its own references. The completion join and the plan-id adopter are unchanged.
narratives.Overview:
1. Story issue of a brief. The story issue of a brief is the one issue the completion identity join anchors on (`resolvePlanGithubIssueRef`). The closing-keywords check and the story-line writer read it through that same function.
2. Identity agreement. For a running brief that would require a line under item 3, the check takes the owner list the plan-id adopter uses for the story issue: every brief in `xbrief/active`, whatever its status, for which `briefOwnsIssue` is true for the repository-scoped issue (`adoptPlanIdFromOwnedIssue` builds this list). The check fails for that brief in two cases only. Case A: the list holds a brief other than this one; the message names the story issue and each such brief. Case B: the list is empty and `briefOwnsIssue` is true for this brief and another issue among its own references; the message names both issues and the repair: make the owned issue the first GitHub issue reference of the brief. In every other case the story issue is usable: the list holds only this brief, or the list is empty and this brief owns none of its references by that predicate. No line satisfies the requirement in case A or case B.
3. One required line per running brief. In `evaluateStoryLineRequirement`, a running brief that names this PR as `metadata.productPullRequest` requires one line, for its story issue. A body reference (Refs, Tracking, Related) to an issue N requires a line for the story issue of the running brief that N belongs to: N itself when N is the story issue of a running brief; otherwise the story issue of the one running brief that names N as a reference. When more than one running brief names N and none has N as its story issue, the requirement for N is as today.
4. Either line kind satisfies the requirement, as today: `deft-story: <story issue>` or `deft-story-part: <story issue>`. The conflict rule for both lines on one number and the lands-with-product rule are unchanged.
5. Writer. `--write-story-line` for a brief writes one line, for the story issue of that brief, and no line for the other issues the brief names. For a brief whose story issue is not valid under item 2 it writes nothing and prints the message of item 2.
6. Message. The missing-line message names the story issue and the brief, and says that the other issues the brief names need no line.
7. Unchanged. The completion identity join (`verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity`, `proveSoleMarkBasis`, the competitor scan) and the plan-id adopter are not changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running brief that names three issues, owns the first of them and names this PR as its product PR, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs on a body with the one line `deft-story: <story issue>`, then it passes.
- Given that merged PR and body, when the completion identity join runs for the brief, then it admits the PR on the mark basis with no operator grant.
- Given that body and several running briefs, when the plan-id adopter runs, then it resolves that brief.
- Given a running brief that names three issues and owns the first, when the story-line writer runs for it, then the body gains exactly one story line, for the story issue.
- Given a running brief that owns its first issue reference and a second brief in `xbrief/active` that is not running and owns the same issue, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs for the first brief's product PR, then it fails and the message carries the lookup's reason.
- Given a running brief whose ingest note names its first issue reference by number only, with no repository, and that names two further issues, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs on a body with the one line for the first issue, then it passes.
- Given a running single-reference brief with no ingest origin and no plan-id binding, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` and the story-line writer run, then each result is the same as today.
- Given running brief A with no ingest origin and no plan-id binding whose first issue reference is owned by running brief B, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs for A's product PR with the one line for that issue, then it fails and the message names B.
- Given a running brief with no ingest origin and no plan-id binding that names three issues, none owned by any brief, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs on a body with the one line for its story issue, then it passes, and the completion identity join admits the merged PR on the mark basis.
- Given a running brief whose first issue reference is not the issue it owns and that no brief owns, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs for its product PR, then it fails and the message names both issues and the repair.
- Given a running brief whose first issue reference is owned by another running brief, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs for its product PR, then it fails with that message.
- Given either of those two briefs, when the story-line writer runs, then it writes no line and prints that message.
- Given a body that names a further issue of a running brief with `Refs` and carries no story line, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs, then it fails and the message names the story issue of that brief.
- Given a body with `deft-story:` marks for the story issues of two different running briefs, when the completion identity join runs, then its mark basis refuses as today.
- Given a single-issue brief made by `issue:ingest`, when each check runs, then the result is the same as today.
narratives.Constraint:
- Accepting several `deft-story:` marks in the identity join when a brief names them all (comment 6933463009 finding 1: a reference is not ownership).
- A new marker for further issues of a brief.
- `deft-story-part:` lines for the further issues as the documented form (comment 6933463009 findings 2 and 3).
- Changing the join anchor or the plan-id adopter in this story (comment 6933560705 finding 1 names it as the larger alternative).
- A second way of counting owners inside the story-line check (comment 6933615059 finding 1).
- Refusing a brief only because it has no ownership record, or a repair text that cannot apply to it (comment 6933615059 finding 2).
- Letting a brief with no ownership record skip the lookup (comment 6934615896 finding 1).
- A rule that depends on whether a brief "has an ownership record" (comment 6934685978 finding 1).
- Any change to the mark basis, the other bases of the join, or operator attestation.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer completing a story whose brief names several issues, I want the closing-keywords check and the story-line writer to ask for the one line the completion step anchors on, so that the product PR passes both checks and completes with no operator grant.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. New packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/story-issue.ts: storyIssueOfBrief(plan, repo) reads resolvePlanGithubIssueRef (same-repository anchor; otherwise today's storyIssuesOfBrief rule for briefs with no GitHub issue reference) and evaluateStoryIssueIdentity(projectRoot, briefPath, plan, repo) applies Bound item 2 with the adopter's owner list (listActiveBriefEntries + briefOwnsIssue), returning usable or a case A / case B message.
2. packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts: evaluateStoryLineRequirement maps each body reference and each productPullRequest brief to one required story issue (Bound item 3), fails case A / case B briefs with the identity message, and words the missing-line message per Bound item 6; storyIssuesForBranch and writeStoryLineToBodyFile write one line per brief and nothing for a case A / case B brief (Bound item 5). 3. Tests: packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/story-issue.test.ts covers clauses 8-22 (check, writer, adopter, completion identity join on temp projects); main.test.ts is adjusted only where today's multi-line expectation changes.
4. Docs: content/scm/github.md story-line rule gains one sentence (one line per brief, for its first GitHub issue reference); changelog.d/6468-one-story-line.md.

## Problem

A story brief that names more than one issue cannot pass both `pr:check-closing-keywords` and the completion identity join. Closing-keywords asks for a `deft-story:` line for every issue the PR body names. The identity join asks for one sole `deft-story: N` mark. A PR cannot do both, so the operator must mint a `delivery-identity-attest` grant.

## Evidence

- `evaluateStoryLineRequirement` (`packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts` ~1025-1080, origin/master `7aef28cb5`): for each issue the body names with Refs / Tracking / Related that has a running brief, and for each issue of a running brief that names this PR as `metadata.productPullRequest`, a `deft-story: N` or `deft-story-part: N` line is required (#6316).
- `proveSoleMarkBasis` (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts` ~1213-1235): basis (a) needs `soleDeftStoryMark(body) === issueNumber`. A body with several `deft-story:` lines has no sole mark, so basis (a) fails (#6317). Basis (b), a closing keyword, is pushed to Refs by the #3781 closeout gate (#6310).
- 2026-11-16: the small-items story (#6421 with #6410 and #6412). Product PR #6457 carried three `deft-story:` lines to pass closing-keywords. Finalize then refused the identity join. The operator minted `delivery-identity-attest` for #6457 at `1d352d69c` (reported by a worker, not re-read). Completion is still open in #6464.
- Related, different class: #6198 (productPullRequest stamp coherence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running brief that names several issues, when its product PR body carries the lines closing-keywords asks for, then the completion identity join admits the PR with no operator grant.
- Given that same PR body, when `pr:check-closing-keywords` runs, then it passes.
- Given a PR with marks for two unrelated stories, when the identity join runs, then it still refuses as today.

Possible directions: lines for secondary issues use a distinct marker that the join ignores, or the join accepts the brief's origin issue mark among several marks that all belong to the same brief.
